questions.stemMarkdown:
A retailer schedules a daily competitor-price report. The agreed outcome is a dated comparison file in the team folder, covering the listed products or explicitly stating that no prices could be checked. Staff must review it before using it for pricing decisions.

Today the task dashboard says:

> Run completed.

The reviewer has not located today’s report and has no evidence about its coverage or delivery. Yesterday’s file is present. She must decide what the status proves and what to check next.

Which assessment and next check best fit the current evidence?

options.textMarkdown: Treat the completed status as success and use yesterday’s report for continuity, asking the next run to explain any changed competitor prices it discovers.
Treat the status as execution evidence; locate today’s output and check its date, coverage, or explicit no-data result in the destination before accepting success.
Treat the missing report as proof that no prices changed, and record a no-change result in the folder so the report sequence remains complete.
Treat the missing report as proof that the prompt is inadequate, rewrite its output instructions now, and rerun the schedule before inspecting the run.

questions.explanationMarkdown: A completed run is not evidence of a correct, complete, delivered outcome. Check the observable success signal and actual destination, without inferring no updates or an instruction failure solely from silence.

optionExplanations.A: Carries forward an old file without establishing today’s required outcome.
optionExplanations.B: Treats status as run evidence and looks for the dated, covered, delivered outcome or explicit no-data result.
optionExplanations.C: No located file is not evidence of no price change or no data.
optionExplanations.D: Prematurely diagnoses prompt failure before locating outcome evidence or examining the current run.

sources.courseTitle: General Agents on the Web: A Crash Course
sources.sectionHeading: Ran is not the same as worked

questions.stemMarkdown:
An agency used AI to write a script that combines monthly campaign exports. The script applies the agreed cancelled-campaign rule and produces the required totals and exceptions. It passed a small hand-checked sample and full-file checks.

The file structure and rules are expected to stay the same next month. A covering analyst will need to repeat the job. The creator wants the tested behavior and its purpose to survive between chats, rather than requesting fresh code from memory each month. No automatic schedule is needed.

Which handover best supports repeatable use of the tested solution?

options.textMarkdown: Keep the script file with a plain-language header, its brief, and the known-answer sample in one task folder; rerun it on new matching exports.
Keep the current results and ask the covering analyst to recreate the script from those totals, comparing each report with the previous month’s output.
Save the brief as a reusable prompting Skill and generate a new script each month, using the same instructions to preserve behavior across analysts.
Save the conversation link and current report in the Project, having the covering analyst continue that thread whenever an export needs the same transformation.

questions.explanationMarkdown: Preserve the executable script, human intent, and a ready known-answer test together. This makes the stable transformation rerunnable and explainable to a covering colleague without regenerated code or private session dependence.

optionExplanations.A: Retains tested executable behavior with intent and a known-answer sample for repeat use and handover.
optionExplanations.B: Output examples do not preserve the implemented rules, source code, or a valid known-answer test for a different month’s data.
optionExplanations.C: Reuses intention but regenerates implementation, losing the specifically requested tested behavior between runs.
optionExplanations.D: A conversation/report does not explicitly preserve a runnable script plus intent and sample for a clean handover.

sources.courseTitle: Code You Never Write
sources.sectionHeading: 8. Keep the script: a solved problem becomes a button

questions.stemMarkdown:
A club has built a Skill for monthly activity summaries. Its instructions define four sections, expense grouping, and how to report a month with no activities. A normal test loads the Skill and produces the correct summary.

The release checklist currently shows:

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Normal month | Passed |
| Empty month | Not tried |
| Messy expense entries | Not tried |
| Unrelated short message | Not tried |

The club wants colleagues to reuse it. The tested procedure has not been changed, and no other release checks have been performed.

Which next test plan best addresses the remaining release evidence?

options.textMarkdown: Run the normal month repeatedly with different wording, approving team use if the four-section layout stays consistent across all of those successful summary requests.
Ask a stronger model to inspect the instructions and score clarity, approving team use if it finds no contradiction in the written empty-month rule.
Test empty and messy inputs against the rules and try the unrelated request for non-activation; repair observed failures and rerun the checks before reuse.
Release the Skill to a small group using normal months, asking colleagues to report any empty-month or messy-input problems when they eventually encounter them.

questions.explanationMarkdown: A successful ordinary run leaves awkward-case behavior and negative activation untested. Exercise those stated cases before reuse, checking outputs against explicit rules and returning observed failures for targeted repair.

optionExplanations.A: Rephrased ordinary successes do not test the omitted data and negative-trigger cases.
optionExplanations.B: Instruction review is useful but not execution evidence for empty/messy outputs or unrelated requests.
optionExplanations.C: Tests the actual untried awkward inputs and unrelated request, then repairs/retests observed failures.
optionExplanations.D: A live pilot delays the known missing checks until colleagues encounter the cases.

sources.courseTitle: Skills & Connectors: Teach AI Once, Connect It to Your Apps
sources.sectionHeading: 13. Test, then iterate

questions.stemMarkdown:
A library uses AI to draft a reading-club announcement. Its prompt says:

> Write a friendly post promoting our holiday reading club.

The draft praises reading. The librarian calls it “too generic”. The intended readers are busy parents of children aged seven to ten. The desired next step is to register through the supplied sign-up page before Friday; the club details and link are already available.

She wants feedback that changes the next draft in an observable way, rather than another request to make it better.

Which TWO additions together turn that feedback into useful directions?

options.textMarkdown: Make the announcement warm and persuasive, using vivid language about reading so the revised post feels less generic to the people who see it.
Write for busy parents of children aged seven to ten, explaining the club’s relevant benefit using the details rather than general praise of reading.
Keep the message under a word limit and add varied sentence openings, so the librarian can judge whether its style has become more distinctive.
Give three alternative versions with different tones and ask the librarian to choose the strongest one, leaving the announcement’s content priorities to each draft.
End with a clear request to register through the supplied sign-up page before Friday, using the link so readers can take that next step.

questions.explanationMarkdown: Translate reaction into checkable content requirements: a specified audience and the intended action. Other changes may improve craft but leave what should be present unsettled.

optionExplanations.A: Warmer/persuasive language repeats a subjective reaction without identifying the audience-specific content or next action.
optionExplanations.B: Gives concrete audience and relevant benefit from supplied details.
optionExplanations.C: Length and sentence variety are measurable but do not address the stated audience/registration goal.
optionExplanations.D: Tone alternatives are useful but leave the content priorities that caused genericness unspecified.
optionExplanations.E: Gives a concrete registration action, channel, deadline, and existing link.

sources.courseTitle: Workflow Design & Diagnosis
sources.sectionHeading: 13. Turn a reaction into an instruction

questions.stemMarkdown:
An administrator asks AI to compare two ventilation units. AI recommends one and supplies quotations from the manufacturers’ specifications. The administrator confirms that the quotations are copied accurately and that the units’ prices are correct.

The recommendation also assumes that the chosen unit’s technical capacity fits the building. The administrator cannot assess that technical assumption. A qualified facilities engineer can review the specifications and building requirements before purchase. She needs to decide what verification remains before accepting the recommendation.

Which check best addresses the remaining basis for the recommendation?

options.textMarkdown: Run the same comparison through another model family, accepting the recommendation if both models select the same unit and cite the same manufacturer specifications.
Have the engineer assess the capacity assumption against the building requirements and specifications, then reconsider the recommendation using that review before choosing the unit.
Recheck every quoted sentence and price against the original pages, accepting the recommendation if those factual details remain correct throughout the complete comparison.
Ask AI to explain the capacity assumption in simpler language and score its confidence, letting the administrator accept it once the explanation is clear.

questions.explanationMarkdown: Correct quotations do not validate the applicability assumption that carries the recommendation. Use the available relevant expertise to assess that assumption against the actual requirements before accepting the conclusion.

optionExplanations.A: Model agreement does not replace expertise on the unverified technical applicability.
optionExplanations.B: Relevant available expertise checks the unverified capacity assumption against actual building requirements before purchase.
optionExplanations.C: Already checked extraction/price accuracy does not settle suitability for the building.
optionExplanations.D: Comprehensibility and confidence are not expert validation of technical fit.

sources.sectionHeading: 3. Feel what it is like to be a non-expert

questions.stemMarkdown:
An employee preparing a summary accidentally uploads a named customer list through a personal account rather than the required managed route. She notices it immediately. No colleague has received the summary, and she does not know whether the uploaded data went onward.

The company has an incident channel and an owner who directs evidence handling and any notifications. A colleague suggests deleting the chat first, then reporting that the data was removed. She needs to respond before creating further copies.

Which immediate response best fits the incident process?

options.textMarkdown: Delete the chat and customer list first, then report the remaining risk once visible copies are gone and the summary has been recreated safely.
Ask the provider whether the list was retained, waiting for its answer before reporting so the incident owner receives an account of the exposure.
Send the uploaded list to an internal group for advice, asking colleagues to identify which customer details need removal before raising a formal incident.
Stop further copying, record the known data, route, time, and uncertainty, report promptly through the incident channel, and follow the owner’s evidence-handling instructions.

questions.explanationMarkdown: Contain spread, record factual knowns and unknowns, and report promptly without waiting for certainty. The incident owner controls evidence/deletion/notification decisions; deleting a visible chat does not prove data removal.

optionExplanations.A: Unilateral deletion may damage evidence and does not establish provider deletion; reporting is delayed by cleanup.
optionExplanations.B: Investigation may be useful but does not justify waiting to report known exposure.
optionExplanations.C: Creates unnecessary new copies and bypasses the defined incident path.
optionExplanations.D: Contains spread, records known/unknown facts, reports promptly, and follows the owner’s handling instructions.

questions.stemMarkdown:
A retailer has two jobs. The first matches 1,500 stock records with a returns export and produces exact item totals using an agreed rule. The second drafts one courteous reply explaining an approved delivery delay to a customer.

The files and rules are ready. Facts and the approved remedy for the reply are supplied. Neither job needs external research. The manager is choosing an approach for each job; she wants computed data results and an appropriately worded draft, with checks before either is used.

Which pairing best fits the work required?

options.textMarkdown: Use a strong reasoning chat for both jobs, asking it to explain the stock totals and then adapt that reasoning to the customer’s reply.
Use code execution for both jobs, turning the approved delay facts into a fixed template while asking the program to determine courteous wording.
Use executed code to match and total the stock records, and conversational drafting for the reply; check both outputs against their supplied requirements.
Use conversational analysis to identify the stock pattern first and compute only if anomalies appear, while using code to choose the customer reply’s wording.

questions.explanationMarkdown: Bulk exact matching/totals signal code execution. A single courteous explanation grounded in supplied facts is a drafting judgment. Choose by work type and verify each outcome, rather than routing both by one preferred tool.

optionExplanations.A: Fluent reasoning does not replace execution for 1,500 records and exact totals.
optionExplanations.B: Code can instantiate a template, but determining courteous wording is the conversational drafting need, not an exact data transformation.
optionExplanations.C: Matches each job to computation or conversational drafting and checks both supplied requirements.
optionExplanations.D: Defers required exact processing and routes wording judgment toward an inappropriate computational selection method.

sources.courseTitle: Code You Never Write
sources.sectionHeading: 3. The dividing line: which problems are code problems

questions.stemMarkdown:
A team wants a weekly AI news brief while the coordinator’s laptop is off. An attended trial used the approved cloud news sources and produced a report, but saved it in a folder on that laptop.

The schedule has a Monday start time and a named reviewer before circulation. An approved cloud folder is available. Nobody has specified how an empty week should be reported or how staff will distinguish a delivered report from a run that merely completed. No unattended trial has been performed.

Which preparation best closes the remaining design gaps before scheduling regular runs?

options.textMarkdown: Use the cloud folder as the output destination, define the empty-week result and success signal, then test the route twice with the laptop off.
Keep the trial’s local destination and add a completion notification, letting the reviewer open the file when the coordinator next turns on the laptop.
Schedule the trial’s existing steps and have the reviewer request a brief if Monday’s file is missing, preserving the method that produced good content.
Move the destination to the cloud folder and enable the clock, relying on completion status to distinguish an empty week from a missing report.

questions.explanationMarkdown: Unattended workflow design must account for all reachable sources/destinations, observable outcome signals, authority and empty cases. A closes the local dependency and missing outcome semantics, then tests the route under the actual device-off condition.

optionExplanations.A: Closes offline destination dependency and empty/success criteria, then tests the revised device-off route twice.
optionExplanations.B: A local destination depends on the offline device; completion notification does not prove delivery or define empty outcomes.
optionExplanations.C: Uses reactive human reruns instead of closing known dependency and success/empty-case gaps before scheduling.
optionExplanations.D: Fixes reach but still treats runtime completion as the missing outcome definition and leaves empty/missing ambiguous.

sources.sectionHeading: The four answers before you schedule

sources.courseTitle: General Agents on the Web: A Crash Course
sources.sectionHeading: Walk it before you schedule it

questions.stemMarkdown:
An analyst has a reusable stock-summary method that works when pasted into chat. She wants colleagues to install it as a Skill using the course’s package structure, rather than copy its prompt manually.

Her folder contains:

```text
stock-summary/
  guide.md
```

The document has valid name and description frontmatter followed by the tested instructions. There are no required external assets or scripts. The name is stock-summary, and its description names the intended requests. She is choosing the smallest packaging correction while preserving that working content.

Which correction makes this package match the required structure?

options.textMarkdown: Keep guide.md and add a note in its description saying that it is the main file, allowing the loader to discover instructions from metadata.
Rename the folder to SKILL.md and keep guide.md inside it, using the folder name to identify the method while preserving the tested document unchanged.
Export guide.md as a PDF and attach it to each colleague’s Project, treating that reference as the installed Skill whenever a summary is requested.
Rename guide.md to SKILL.md inside stock-summary, retaining its valid frontmatter and instructions, then check the resulting package before handing it to colleagues.

questions.explanationMarkdown: The required main file is exactly SKILL.md inside the correctly named Skill folder. The content and folder already fit; rename the actual file, not its folder or a reference document.

optionExplanations.A: Description cannot substitute for the required canonical main filename.
optionExplanations.B: Changes the folder rather than placing the required file inside a kebab-case folder.
optionExplanations.C: A Project reference can support prompting but is not an installable Skill package.
optionExplanations.D: Corrects the actual filename while retaining already valid method and metadata.

sources.courseTitle: Skills & Connectors: Teach AI Once, Connect It to Your Apps
sources.sectionHeading: 11. Anatomy of a SKILL.md

questions.stemMarkdown:
Before asking AI, an organiser records:

> Choose the forty-seat room. Confidence: 70%. Switch to the larger room if confirmed registrations exceed forty.

AI then reports forty-six confirmed registrations from the booking file. The organiser checks that count herself and chooses the larger room. On the day, forty-three people attend.

She considers replacing her original note with “I expected more than forty”. The original note, checked count, and actual attendance are available. She wants an honest record of her judgment and the evidence that changed it.

Which review note best preserves that record?

options.textMarkdown: Replace the initial expectation with more than forty, because the final room choice and actual attendance show that this was the judgment she reached.
Retain the original position and confidence, record the verified count that triggered reversal, and compare the expectation with attendance without rewriting her earlier belief.
Retain the forty-seat position but describe the larger-room choice as unexplained AI influence, because changing after the assistant’s answer invalidates an independent judgment.
Record only the successful final room choice and attendance, removing the confidence and earlier position so the audit focuses on results rather than guesses.

questions.explanationMarkdown: A prediction lock preserves a pre-AI position and reversal condition, making later changes and gaps visible. The checked count triggered the predefined change; preserving the original note enables honest learning without hindsight revision.

optionExplanations.A: Rewrites the prior belief after the evidence/outcome and removes the comparison the lock protects.
optionExplanations.B: Preserves prior position/confidence and documents the verified count that met the pre-set reversal condition.
optionExplanations.C: A fact checked by the human met the predefined reversal condition; changing is not automatically blind deference.
optionExplanations.D: Deletes the original position and confidence needed to assess how the judgment developed.

sources.courseTitle: How to Think in the AI Era: Crash Course
sources.sectionHeading: Discipline 1: The Prediction Lock

questions.stemMarkdown:
A charity wants AI to guarantee the exact total of donations it will receive next month. The brief and historical data have been checked. Fresh sessions and a capable model using code still return different precise forecasts. The configuration is current.

Next month’s total is not yet committed or received. The coordinator accepts that prompt, context, feature, and configuration checks have not produced a dependable exact answer. She needs a planning result the team can use rather than another unsupported guarantee.

Which change best addresses the remaining problem?

options.textMarkdown: Gather additional history and ask the model to reconcile its forecasts into an exact total, treating agreement after the larger input as the guarantee.
Increase reasoning effort and require each forecasting step to be explained, using the detailed calculation as the basis for the charity’s exact funding guarantee.
Replace the exact guarantee with a range or adjustable driver model, state the assumptions, and examine how planning changes under different donation outcomes.
Reset the session with a brief and the same data, accepting the first precise forecast that remains unchanged when the assistant repeats its explanation.

questions.explanationMarkdown: After cheaper checks, question task fit: no tool or prompt can guarantee an exact unknown future total from historical data. A range/driver model with explicit assumptions gives a testable planning aid without inventing certainty.

optionExplanations.A: Additional historical evidence may improve forecasting but agreement does not guarantee unknown future receipts.
optionExplanations.B: Transparent or longer reasoning does not turn a forecast into an exact future fact.
optionExplanations.C: Reshapes the unrealistic guarantee into conditional planning with explicit assumptions.
optionExplanations.D: Repetition and another fresh session do not resolve the already-tested task expectation mismatch.

sources.courseTitle: Workflow Design & Diagnosis
sources.sectionHeading: 12. The sequence runs cheapest first

questions.stemMarkdown:
A community group reviewed an AI event summary. Dates and roles are confirmed, but two supplier prices are marked “unverified”. The incoming volunteer coordinator will not have access to the chat.

The group wants a downloadable one-page handover containing the schedule, named responsibilities, and open checks. Its prompt says:

> Summarise our discussion neatly for the new coordinator.

The content is ready for conversion, and no new research is requested. The organiser is revising the brief so the handover retains its unresolved items.

Which TWO additions together best specify the required handover?

options.textMarkdown: Create a downloadable one-page file with a schedule, responsibility table, and open-checks section, providing context for the coordinator to use it without the chat.
Return a concise chat answer with the key dates and roles first, letting the new coordinator request additional details from the organiser when needed.
Use the discussed supplier prices in the budget table without their uncertainty labels, moving unresolved questions to a private note for the departing organiser.
Keep both unverified price labels beside their figures and include the corresponding checks in the handover, keeping confirmed roles and dates as confirmed information.
Produce an introductory paragraph and a link to this conversation, keeping the schedule and unresolved prices in the chat to avoid crowding the document.

questions.explanationMarkdown: Specify a portable artifact and usable structure, and preserve caveats when moving content from chat to document. The absent chat audience needs both confirmed responsibilities and visible unresolved checks in the file.

optionExplanations.A: Specifies the standalone downloadable artifact and required usable structure.
optionExplanations.B: Chat answer and later questions do not provide the requested standalone downloadable handover.
optionExplanations.C: Hides uncertainty from the new user and misrepresents unverified prices as settled.
optionExplanations.D: Preserves both uncertainty labels and open checks while keeping confirmed information distinct.
optionExplanations.E: Depends on chat access that the new coordinator does not have and omits required content from the file.

sources.courseTitle: Just Delegate It: A Crash Course
sources.sectionHeading: 6. Ask for the Deliverable, Not an Answer

questions.stemMarkdown:
An analyst receives a report-formatting extension from another team in her company. Its description promises layout changes only. Package inspection shows a cleanup script that can delete older files. The session where she would enable it has write access to several client folders.

Her task only needs one draft report. The extension’s author confirms that its script uses the session’s file access, rather than a separate task-only scope. Nothing has run yet. She is reviewing the package before use.

Which review best addresses the capability before enabling it?

options.textMarkdown: Test the extension on a sample report within the current session, then approve it if the resulting layout matches the team’s usual report format.
Clarify the cleanup behavior and assess its actual session reach against the one-report task, requiring suitable limits or removing unnecessary actions before enabling it.
Confirm the internal author’s identity and keep the existing session access, using the extension’s formatting description as the boundary for what it may do.
Run a package security scan and enable the extension if it passes, logging cleanup so the analyst can review deletions afterward.

questions.explanationMarkdown: Review source, actual reach, task fit and consequential actions, not just publisher familiarity or description. The known cleanup behavior with broad write access is disproportionate to one draft report and must be constrained before enablement.

optionExplanations.A: Layout success in a broad live session does not establish safe/proportionate deletion reach.
optionExplanations.B: Checks known cleanup actions and actual session reach against the one-report need before enablement.
optionExplanations.C: Internal identity and description do not narrow the actual session access that the author confirmed.
optionExplanations.D: Scanning is not task/data appropriateness approval, and after-action logs do not prevent unnecessary deletion.

sources.courseTitle: Governance, Risk & Responsible Use: A Crash Course
sources.sectionHeading: 3.1 Treat extensions like software, not like prompts

questions.stemMarkdown:
A consulting team requires finished research files in its own approved document folder. The report’s content has passed review, and the assistant reports that the file is saved.

The location inventory shows:

| Copy | Location |
| --- | --- |
| Draft | Temporary task workspace |
| Finished report | Permanent assistant-account storage |
| Firm’s document folder | No report copy |

The team can reopen the account copy after the task ends, and an authorized save route to its document folder is available. It is assessing whether the agreed destination requirement is complete.

Which assessment and next action best match these facts?

options.textMarkdown: The finished copy is already durable, so share its account link with colleagues and mark the firm-folder requirement complete without creating another report copy.
The report is lost when the task ends because its draft is temporary; regenerate the content before saving in the firm’s document folder.
The report is durable in the assistant account, but the firm’s destination requirement remains unmet; save it there and verify its presence and identity.
Move the finished report into the temporary workspace and label it final, using the completion record as evidence that the firm holds its research.

questions.explanationMarkdown: Permanent platform storage is distinct from temporary task space, but neither is the firm’s specified system of record. The finished copy is not lost; deliver it through the authorized route and verify the intended copy.

optionExplanations.A: Durability in the vendor account does not satisfy the explicitly required firm destination.
optionExplanations.B: Transfers the draft’s temporary status to a separately permanent finished copy, inventing loss.
optionExplanations.C: Recognizes platform durability and the still-unmet firm destination, then saves and verifies the right copy.
optionExplanations.D: A final label in temporary space does not change custody or satisfy the firm destination.

sources.courseTitle: General Agents on the Web: A Crash Course
sources.sectionHeading: 5. The three file tiers: where does the deliverable actually live?

questions.stemMarkdown:
A service company wants AI support for routine contract amendments. The data route is approved, and AI can prepare drafts from the relevant records. The workflow contains:

| Step | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Draft | Prepare proposed wording for review |
| Approve | Decide whether the amendment is acceptable |
| Release | Sign and send the agreed amendment |

The manager is accountable for approval. Drafts are reversible; signed and sent commitments cannot simply be withdrawn. A named manager can judge every proposal before it acts. The company is assigning ownership to each step.

Which ownership arrangement best fits the stated workflow?

options.textMarkdown: Keep all three steps human-owned because the manager remains accountable, allowing AI to explain amendment terminology without preparing wording used in the review.
Let AI draft and approve changes matching old examples; have the manager handle signature and sending after checking document identifiers and recipient details.
Let AI draft and release proposals after automatic comparison with the records, having the manager review the commitments afterward to confirm accountability remains human.
Use AI to prepare drafts for the manager’s judgment, while keeping the approval decision and signed release human-owned before a commitment is sent.

questions.explanationMarkdown: Decide step ownership by reversibility, stakes and accountability. Reversible wording can be an AI input judged by a named human; the approval call and irreversible signed release remain human-owned in this stated workflow.

optionExplanations.A: Accountability does not prohibit delegating a reversible input that the responsible person judges.
optionExplanations.B: Moves the approval decision itself to AI on similarity/test performance rather than the required human judging step.
optionExplanations.C: Releases commitments before the human judgment, leaving no gate carrying the consequential approval.
optionExplanations.D: Keeps reversible draft production as input while the human owns the approval call and signed release.

sources.courseTitle: Workflow Design & Diagnosis
sources.sectionHeading: 5. Three criteria decide every step

questions.stemMarkdown:
A coordinator has three proposals and agreed comparison criteria. Some proposals omit support hours. She wants to inspect the extracted facts before they influence a comparison or recommendation; absent terms must remain visible rather than be guessed.

Her prompt says:

> Select the best vendor from these proposals. Explain your choice and include a table of price, contract length, exit terms, and support hours.

No work has started. The proposals are the permitted evidence, and the criteria are complete. She is revising how the work proceeds.

Which TWO additions together best establish the required process?

options.textMarkdown: Rank the vendors first using the agreed criteria, then build a facts table for the preferred proposal so the coordinator can inspect its evidence.
Extract and score all three proposals in one response, using a final self-check of the tables before presenting the recommendation for the coordinator’s approval.
For now, extract the same requested facts from all three proposals into a table and stop, letting the coordinator check source entries before comparison.
Estimate omitted support hours from similar vendor offers and label the estimates, keeping every proposal complete so the scoring method remains easy to apply.
Mark unstated terms as absent and limit later comparisons to the checked table and agreed criteria, keeping unresolved information visible in any subsequent recommendation.

questions.explanationMarkdown: Stage extraction first because its errors propagate. C creates a stop for actual source checking before downstream analysis; E prevents missing data being filled and confines later claims to verified inputs and the given criteria.

optionExplanations.A: Chooses the conclusion before the required extraction review and narrows evidence to the winner.
optionExplanations.B: Self-check in a combined pass is not the coordinator’s required inspection before comparison/recommendation.
optionExplanations.C: Extracts the requested facts across proposals and pauses before they propagate downstream.
optionExplanations.D: Outside offers cannot supply unstated terms in these permitted proposals, even when labeled estimates.
optionExplanations.E: Preserves gaps and constrains later comparisons to checked facts and the given criteria.

questions.stemMarkdown:
A facilitator wants AI to turn a whiteboard process map into a written sequence with its decision branches. A photo shows the large boxes and connecting arrows clearly, but several small labels are blurred. A typed note lists the box names only, without their connections.

The facilitator can supply clear close-up photos of the blurred labels. The assistant can accept text and images. The task needs the real map’s relationships and exact labels, not a newly imagined process. She is choosing the inputs.

Which input approach best matches the evidence needed?

options.textMarkdown: Provide the typed box names and describe the general topic, asking a reasoning model to reconstruct likely connections before writing the sequence and branches.
Provide the whole-map photo plus clear label close-ups and the typed names as a cross-check, flagging remaining uncertainty rather than inferring exact text.
Provide the whole-map photo alone and ask for a polished sequence, accepting reconstructed small labels when they fit the surrounding boxes and arrows.
Use image generation to redraw the blurred photograph more clearly, then have AI transcribe that improved drawing as evidence of the original process branches.

questions.explanationMarkdown: Use images for the actual spatial/arrow relationships and clearer source images/text for exact labels. Neither plausible inference nor a generated redraw supplies reliable original content; uncertainty should remain visible.

optionExplanations.A: Box names omit the relationships; reconstructing likely links invents rather than reads the map.
optionExplanations.B: Combines original relationship photo with exact readable label evidence and uncertainty handling.
optionExplanations.C: Clear large shapes do not make blurred exact labels reliable; meaningful guesses still need checking.
optionExplanations.D: Generated visual cleanup can invent/change labels and links and is not independent source evidence.

questions.stemMarkdown:
An archive team uses one shared Project to summarise donated letters. Summaries must distinguish stated dates from staff estimates. The same correction has been made in the original researcher’s chats repeatedly, and her latest summary follows it.

A covering researcher opens a new chat in the same Project and gets dates presented without that distinction. No shared instruction states the rule. The team wants the discovered correction to be visible and reusable for anyone doing this work, without depending on the original researcher’s conversation history.

Which configuration change best preserves the correction for the team?

options.textMarkdown: Ask the original researcher’s assistant to remember the correction more strongly, then have covering researchers continue their normal Project chats without a shared rule.
Save one corrected summary as a reference example, asking the assistant to copy its date wording even when later letters contain different date evidence.
Have each researcher paste the correction into every new chat, relying on the original researcher to remind covering staff when the omission appears again.
Write an explicit Project standing instruction to label stated and estimated dates, then check a covering-user run against letters containing both kinds of evidence.

questions.explanationMarkdown: A repeated behavioral correction belongs in readable shared configuration, not private memory/history or reminders. State the general rule and verify it in the covering workflow; one example can illustrate but does not replace the explicit requirement.

optionExplanations.A: Personal memory does not reliably transfer an explicit rule to colleagues’ new chats.
optionExplanations.B: A fixed example’s wording is not the general distinction for differing evidence and can be imitated incorrectly.
optionExplanations.C: Repeats the manual repair habit and still relies on the original person being present.
optionExplanations.D: Stores the known behavioral correction explicitly for all Project users and checks transfer in a new run.

questions.stemMarkdown:
An organiser asks a fast AI setting to plan a programme with several linked staffing and room constraints. The brief is complete, the sources are current, and fresh chats still fail: each revision solves one clash but creates another elsewhere.

Three corrections restated the constraints without improving the overall plan. No missing fact or calculation error has been found. A stronger reasoning setting is available but has not been tried. The organiser wants to preserve the requirements while testing a different capability.

Which intervention best fits the remaining evidence?

options.textMarkdown: Restate the constraints with stronger emphasis in another fresh chat using the fast setting, then compare whether its tone shows attention to the clashes.
Remove one staffing constraint and let the fast setting produce a programme, treating a clash-free result as proof that the original requirements were unnecessary.
Run the complete brief at the stronger reasoning setting, then check the programme against all linked constraints before deciding whether the capability change helped.
Ask the fast setting for a detailed explanation of its latest plan, accepting the revision if it explains each local correction convincingly in isolation.

questions.explanationMarkdown: After complete context/rules and repeated equivalent fixes, escalate the available machine capability for a coupled reasoning task and check the actual result. This is a test, not a guarantee that stronger is always correct.

optionExplanations.A: Repeats an already failed prompt/context strategy and judges tone rather than all constraint outcomes.
optionExplanations.B: Changes the job without authorization and cannot show that the original requirement was unnecessary.
optionExplanations.C: Tests the available stronger reasoning capability under the same complete requirements and verifies all constraints.
optionExplanations.D: Persuasive local explanations do not verify global consistency or test the unused stronger capability.

questions.stemMarkdown:
A training centre asks AI to evaluate attendance after it started sending reminder messages. The report’s source counts have been checked:

| Week | Attendees |
| --- | ---: |
| Before reminders | 40 |
| After reminders | 50 |

AI writes:

> Attendance rose by ten, therefore the reminders caused the increase.

The centre has not compared changes in course availability or other promotion between those weeks. The counts are current, and the report cites the real attendance log. The reviewer is choosing a check of the conclusion, rather than repeating the already completed count verification.

Which check most directly evaluates that conclusion?

options.textMarkdown: Recalculate the increase from the source counts and retain the causal claim if the difference is ten, because the log is authentic and current.
Ask a second model to read the same two counts, accepting the explanation if it agrees that reminders are the likely reason attendance increased.
Inspect other relevant changes and comparative evidence before attributing the increase to reminders, checking whether the supplied observations actually support that causal connection.
Replace “caused” with “may have contributed” and keep the report unchanged, using the softer wording as sufficient verification of the explanation for the increase.

questions.explanationMarkdown: The arithmetic is correct, but a temporal association does not establish the causal link. Test the inference against alternative explanations/comparative evidence. Hedging can state uncertainty honestly but is not itself a check of causation.

optionExplanations.A: Validates an already correct difference, not the missing inferential link.
optionExplanations.B: Agreement on the same inadequate evidence does not establish causation.
optionExplanations.C: Examines relevant changes/comparative evidence to test the missing causal link.
optionExplanations.D: Rephrasing acknowledges uncertainty but does not verify the conclusion asked about.

questions.stemMarkdown:
A company has approved a daily AI workflow that drafts internal answers from public FAQ pages. It uses one model family, reads only those pages, saves in the team folder, and cannot send messages. A supervisor reviews drafts before staff use them.

The team proposes changes. Its governance owner requires review when the approved workflow’s data, capability, model, audience, or consequences change. The original approval is available. The team is deciding which proposals need that review before use, not which should automatically be rejected.

Which THREE proposed changes trigger the stated governance re-check?

options.textMarkdown: Enable the workflow to send its answers to customers, extending it from internal draft preparation to external messages while keeping the basic answer layout.
Repeat the approved daily run tomorrow with the same sources, model, permissions, destination, review arrangements, and purpose, after confirming none of those conditions changed.
Change the heading style in the internal drafts, keeping their content, audience, sources, model, permission scope, destination, and human review exactly as already approved.
Add named employee complaint notes as an input source, using the same model and output format to include this information in the drafted answers.
Switch the workflow to another model family, retaining the same sources and output layout but changing the system that processes information and produces drafts.

questions.explanationMarkdown: A changes external actions/audience/consequences; D changes data type/sensitivity/source; E changes model family. Layout continuity does not carry authorization across these changes. An unchanged approved run and cosmetic heading edit do not alter the stated review-trigger dimensions.

optionExplanations.A: Introduces external sending and customer audience/consequences.
optionExplanations.B: Explicitly preserves all material approved conditions; a new date alone is not a stated trigger.
optionExplanations.C: Only heading style changes; all defined governance trigger dimensions explicitly remain unchanged.
optionExplanations.D: Adds named employee data and a new input type/source beyond public FAQ scope.
optionExplanations.E: Changes the model family, an explicit review-trigger dimension.

questions.stemMarkdown:
Two volunteers want a tool to organise event tasks. Only they will use it. AI has produced a working prototype using sample tasks; the volunteers have only seen screenshots.

They disagree about whether task grouping or the weekly view will help them most. Their shared Project holds task definitions and limits for each revision. Before adding more features, they want evidence from their actual use rather than a choice based only on the prototype’s polished appearance.

Which next step best advances the design loop?

options.textMarkdown: Have both volunteers use the prototype on representative tasks, record friction against shared goals, then refine the design and test the changed version.
Add both preferred views and several related features now, using the screenshots to settle presentation before asking the volunteers to review the tool later.
Ask a stronger model to select the better view from the screenshots, then adopt its recommendation and expand the prototype using the task definitions.
Have the volunteers vote on the screenshot layouts and polish the winning view, treating their preference as evidence that the tool fits their workflow.

questions.explanationMarkdown: A prototype needs actual use feedback against shared goals, followed by refinement and another cycle. Stable context helps compare revisions; screenshots, model preference, or a vote alone cannot supply the missing workflow-use evidence.

optionExplanations.A: Uses actual representative work with intended users, records friction, refines, and retests under shared goals.
optionExplanations.B: Adds scope before observing friction in the current testable prototype.
optionExplanations.C: Model screenshot judgment substitutes for the intended users’ actual working experience.
optionExplanations.D: Visual preference helps design but does not establish real-process fit without use.
